title: Header extensions the viewer never offered are negotiated and emitted in the answer, possibly with colliding IDs
test: tests/whep.test.js: 'createViewerAnswer extmap' (3 tests: 'never writes an extmap the offer did not list, so ids cannot collide', 'writes an extmap only when the offer lists that uri with the id the consumer stamps', 'writes one line per id even when the consumer lists a repeated id'), 'createViewerAnswer rtcp-fb' (2 tests), 'buildViewerRtpCapabilities': 'keeps only the router header extensions the offer lists, per section kind', 'adds no header extension for an offer that lists none', 'limits each codec rtcpFeedback to the feedback the matched offer codec lists, wildcard included', 'does not take codecs or extensions from disabled or send-only sections'; 'offer to answer with consumers shaped like mediasoup builds them' (3 tests); 'parseViewerOffer rtcp-fb': 'keeps a wildcard rtcp-fb line as payload type *'
proof: Before the fix, node --test tests/whep.test.js failed 15 of the 47 tests (the 15 new ones; the 'keeps the router codec and payload type selection' guard passed before and after). The collision case: an offer that binds id 4 to sdes:mid, with a consumer carrying the router's mid (id 1) and abs-send-time (router id 4, never offered), produced 'a=extmap:4 urn:ietf:params:rtp-hdrext:sdes:mid | a=extmap:4 http://www.webrtc.org/experiments/rtp-hdrext/abs-send-time', two lines with id 4 in one m-section. The same run of the real mediasoup ortc code (getConsumableRtpParameters + getConsumerRtpParameters, router from config.MEDIA_CODECS) with a Chrome-like offer (video: toffset 14, abs-send-time 2, video-orientation 13, transport-wide-cc 3, playout-delay 5, mid 4; audio: ssrc-audio-level 1, abs-send-time 2, transport-wide-cc 3, mid 4) answered video extmap 4 mid, 2 abs-send-time, 3 transport-cc, 13 video-orientation, 14 toffset, 5 playout-delay and 12 packet-id (urn:mediasoup:params:rtp-hdrext:packet-id, which no browser offers), and audio 4 mid, 2 abs-send-time, 1 ssrc-audio-level, 11 playout-delay, 12 packet-id, plus 'a=rtcp-fb:111 nack', which the offer never listed. After the fix the answer carries at most what the offer lists: the answer's extmap lines are exactly the consumer's headerExtensions that the offer lists with the same id, no id or uri repeats in a section, rtcp-fb lines are limited to feedback offered for the answered payload type or by wildcard and present on the consumer codec, and buildViewerRtpCapabilities hands out only offered extensions and copies of the router codecs. All 47 tests in tests/whep.test.js pass; npm run lint and typecheck pass; npm test passes 525 of 525.

title: WHEP answer rewrites payload types and header-extension IDs in SDP only, while consumer RTP keeps the router's values
test: tests/whep.test.js: 'buildViewerRtpCapabilities': 'sets preferredId to the offered id, so the consumer drops an extension whose router id differs', 'does not let an extension offered for one kind reach the other kind consumer', 'returns copies and leaves the router capabilities untouched'; 'offer to answer with consumers shaped like mediasoup builds them': 'negotiates every offered extension whose id equals the router id, with consistent ids', 'negotiates no extension for a Chrome-like offer whose ids differ from the router ids, and says nothing unoffered'
proof: Fixed for the header-extension half of the issue; the payload type half is TASK-025 and was not touched. Before the fix, the Chrome-like offer through the real mediasoup ortc code gave a video consumer whose headerExtensions were mid 1, abs-send-time 4, transport-cc 5, video-orientation 8, toffset 9, playout-delay 11, packet-id 12 (the ids the worker stamps on the RTP), while the answer's SDP said mid 4, abs-send-time 2, transport-cc 3, video-orientation 13, toffset 14, playout-delay 5: the same uri under a different number, so Chrome would read the stamped id 5 (transport-cc on the wire) as playout-delay. buildViewerRtpCapabilities passed the router's header extensions and its own codec objects (filteredCodecs.push(rc)) to consume(). After the fix, each capability entry's preferredId is the offered id, so mediasoup keeps a consumer extension only when the offered id equals the id it stamps, and the answer writes only the consumer's extensions the offer lists under that same id; the SDP can no longer disagree with the wire. The same real-ortc run now gives, for the Chrome-like offer, no header extensions on either consumer, an empty extmap list and rtcp-fb limited to nack, nack pli, ccm fir for video; for an offer numbered like the router (mid 1, abs-send-time 4, transport-cc 5, audio-level 6) the video consumer keeps mid 1, abs-send-time 4, transport-cc 5 and the audio consumer mid 1, abs-send-time 4, ssrc-audio-level 6, and the answer lists exactly those. Rollout note: for a Chrome-like offer none of mid, abs-send-time and transport-wide-cc is negotiated any more (their offered ids 4, 2 and 3 differ from the router's 1, 4 and 5), so mediasoup also drops transport-cc and goog-remb feedback for that viewer; before, they were advertised with ids that did not match the RTP.
